title: Routing between VLANs
summary: Let two VLANs talk to each other through VLAN interfaces on a layer 3 switch.
objectives: Place two hosts in different VLANs
Create a VLAN interface that acts as the gateway of each VLAN
See why hosts in different VLANs need a router to talk

tasks.title: Create the VLANs
tasks.description: PC1 belongs to VLAN 10 and PC2 to VLAN 20. Create both VLANs on the switch.

tasks.title: Assign the ports
tasks.description: Put GE0/0/1 (PC1) in VLAN 10 and GE0/0/2 (PC2) in VLAN 20.
hints: Both ports must be access ports.
Example: interface GE0/0/1, then port link-type access, then port default vlan 10

criteria.label: GE0/0/1 is an access port in VLAN 10
GE0/0/2 is an access port in VLAN 20

tasks.title: Create the gateways
tasks.description: Each PC already points at a gateway: 192.0.2.1 for VLAN 10 and 198.51.100.1 for VLAN 20. Create a VLAN interface for each VLAN with that address and a /24 mask.
hints: A VLAN interface is the switch's own address inside a VLAN. It is also the gateway hosts of that VLAN use.
Example: interface vlanif10, then ip address 192.0.2.1 24, then quit, and the same for vlanif20 with 198.51.100.1 24

tasks.title: Verify the routing
tasks.description: The two VLANs must now reach each other through the switch.
hints: If a check fails, confirm each PC sits in the VLAN whose gateway it uses.
